user_prompt: Is the core idea of this paper novel relative to the related work I gave you?
scope: The target paper target/paper.txt (arXiv:2201.11903, Chain-of-Thought Prompting) and the supplied corpus of 10 real related-paper abstracts under corpus/, searched by search_repo and read by inspect_file; the novelty question is scoped to the target's STATED contribution and to subsumption BY THE SUPPLIED CORPUS ONLY (not the open literature).

claims.text: The target paper's stated contribution is identifiable from the supplied text (eliciting multi-step reasoning in a large language model via a few chain-of-thought exemplars supplied in the prompt, with no gradient update to the model).
The contribution is identified (C1) and the closest work in the supplied corpus has been located by search and inspected.

Under the supplied corpus and the declared search protocol, no inspected corpus item subsumes the target's stated contribution (eliciting reasoning purely via few-shot exemplar demonstrations in the prompt, with zero training/fine-tuning of the model): the contribution stands as novel relative to this corpus.

atoms.proposition: The target's contribution paragraph is read via inspect_file over target/paper.txt.
The corpus is searched for the mechanism family with search_repo (pattern step.by.step|scratchpad|intermediate reasoning|chain.of.thought over corpus/), returning at least one match.
The closest-by-mechanism corpus candidate (Scratchpad, arXiv:2112.00114) is read via inspect_file.
The closest prompting-technique corpus candidate (Prompt Programming, arXiv:2102.07350) is read via inspect_file.
Expert adjudication is obtained (ask_user) on whether any inspected corpus abstract claims the target's specific mechanism; the adjudication is that none does.

notes_for_annotators: Target arXiv:2201.11903 (Chain-of-Thought Prompting, Wei et al. 2022), corpus of 10 real abstracts, all fetched 2026-07-29 from arxiv.org abs pages (provenance in artifacts/res-cot/PROVENANCE). ADJUDICATION (E5 answer, verified by reading the abstracts): No corpus item subsumes the target's stated contribution. The target's contribution is a PURE INFERENCE-TIME PROMPTING method -- a few chain-of-thought demonstrations as exemplars in the prompt, no gradient update -- that elicits multi-step reasoning in a sufficiently large off-the-shelf LM. The closest corpus items differ in mechanism: Scratchpad (2112.00114) achieves step-by-step multi-step computation but explicitly by TRAINING transformers to emit intermediate steps ('we train transformers to perform multi-step computations'), i.e. requires fine-tuning, not a frozen-model prompting technique; Prompt Programming (2102.07350) is about general prompt-design techniques (0-shot framing, narrative/cultural anchors, metaprompts) and does not propose exemplar-based step-by-step reasoning demonstrations for arithmetic/commonsense/symbolic reasoning tasks. Self-consistency (2203.11171) and Least-to-most prompting (2205.10625) both postdate the target (March/May 2022 vs January 2022) and are themselves extensions OF chain-of-thought prompting, not prior candidates that could subsume it. Route minimality: E1 necessary (cannot judge novelty without reading the contribution); E2 necessary (the corpus must actually be searched, not assumed); E3, E4 necessary (the two nearest candidates must be read, not inferred from titles); E5 necessary (the subsumption call is the adjudicated conclusion). Order-coherence by containment. Decoy citation_count_lookup is not a listed action. The answer the ask_user tool returns is this note; E5 attests that the adjudication was obtained.
